extractions.value: On neurologic examination, the patient exhibited stiffness and frequent painful extensor spasms of the lower extremities provoked by tactile stimuli and voluntary movement of the extremities. Tone in the upper extremities was normal during passive movements, and there were no spasms or contractures in upper extremity or neck muscles. Passive head movements caused no discomfort. There was no appearance of fixed lumbar hyperlordosis, abnormal trunk extension, rigidity in abdominal muscles, or muscle hypertrophy.

extractions.value: clinical features (stiffness and spasms of lower extremities), amphiphysin antibodies in serum, MRI brain showing T2 hyperintensity in left temporal lobe, radiographic screening disclosing metastatic breast cancer
extractions.quote: On examination, she exhibited severe stiffness and intermittent extensor spasms of the lower extremities. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed T2 hyperintensity in the left temporal lobe with enhancement after gadolinium administration on T1-weighted images. Amphiphysin antibodies were present in the serum. Radiographic screening for malignancy disclosed a metastatic breast cancer.

extractions.value: The case is a unique example of amphiphysin autoimmunity, illustrating the possibility of paraneoplastic stiff-person syndrome and limbic encephalitis coexisting in a patient with a 'classical' presentation of stiff-person syndrome confined to the lower extremities.
